A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIPER research, despite retitling and substantial reorganization. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including visually inspected pages whose content was not captured by text extraction.

before.justification: v3 reports original super-resolution, image-compression and image-regression experiments, plus video super-resolution results and additional ablations in its appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and additionally reports lightweight super-resolution, motion-deblurring, image-dehazing and broader sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The coefficient backbone, Swin basis generator, sawtooth sampling, multi-frequency reconstruction, SR prior and basis-merging procedure remain. Additional backbone and task applications use the existing framework. The convolution omitted from v4's Equation (8) is explicitly a notational simplification.

E1.justification: v4 adds GoPro motion deblurring and Dense-Haze image dehazing in Tables 11–12. Reported SA-1B training is replaced by ImageNet, which already appeared in v3's pretraining comparison. Existing SR, compression and appendix video-SR benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds EDSR, RCAN, CAT-A+, ART and PFT. Table 2 adds SegPIC and LALIC and removes CCA from that comparison, although CCA remains in the rate-distortion plots. Tables 10–12 introduce substantial additional comparator sets for lightweight SR, deblurring and dehazing.

E3.justification: The reported main training setup switches from SA-1B to ImageNet, and the explicit pretraining-dataset control disappears. Added evaluations introduce models below one million parameters, LAM/Diffusion Index measurements and broader controlled hyperparameter configurations. The principal SR budget remains 300k pretraining plus 200k finetuning iterations. These are reported setting changes, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v4 adds pixel-attribution analysis in Figure 1, tests applicability beyond SR/compression, and substantially expands sensitivity testing over N, alpha and alternative coordinate transformations in Tables 13–14. The SA-1B/ImageNet comparison is removed. Existing basis-order, concatenation, SR-prior, factorization and merging ablations are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added, including GoPro PSNR of 34.40 for MLWNet-F versus 33.83 for MLWNet, and Dense-Haze PSNR of 18.12 for ConvIR-F versus 17.45 for ConvIR. Table 1 changes ATD-L Set5 PSNR from 33.12 to 33.15 and removes the separate HAT-F-ImageNet row. Most retained FIPER scores persist despite revised training descriptions. Table 2 largely incorporates averaged timings already present in v3's appendix.

T1.justification: The core Fourier, factorization, reconstruction and compression equations remain mathematically equivalent. Separating the frequency preliminaries, naming the learned basis Mi and removing redundant Factor Fields background formulas do not introduce substantive changes to definitions, derivations, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the stated mergeable-basis application from multi-frame compression and super-resolution to compression. The main contribution statements, generalizability proposition, state-of-the-art claims and headline 204.4% and 9.35% figures otherwise remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations concerning pixel utilization, applicability across restoration tasks and hyperparameter tradeoffs. Appendix F explicitly discusses failure on extremely fine structures absent from LR inputs, while Appendix G proposes future generation applications. The principal frequency-based explanation and real-time decoding limitation remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 specifies sawtooth periods and concrete sampling locations; Appendix D adds an explicit image-token-plus-CLS merging example. Figure 2 newly states parameter-count matching. These clarify existing mechanisms. Conversely, v3's explicit main-text instruction about which modules are frozen during multi-image compression training is omitted.

R1.justification: v4 adds a Spectral Coordinate Transforms discussion and expands positioning against works such as CoordConv, DDRM, Restormer and HiFiC. It also changes the spatially varying coefficient description from being different from previous work to explicitly following Factor Fields. These are substantive positioning and attribution changes.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, methodological explanations and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Frequency preliminaries become a separate section, ablations are consolidated in the appendix, and references move before the supplementary material. The title and numerous captions and explanations also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. Core diagrams are redrawn or combined, the convergence analysis becomes three panels with logarithmic iteration axes, and an attribution figure and five experimental tables are added. Existing diagrams, qualitative examples and ablation tables are also relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: The added applicability and sensitivity evidence, clearer explanations and improved attribution strengthen the paper. However, v4 changes reported pretraining to ImageNet and removes the dataset control while retaining most earlier scores: its HAT-F row matches v3's SA-1B results rather than v3's separate ImageNet row. The PDFs do not explain whether this reflects corrected documentation or changed experiments, and the new task evaluations have sparse implementation details. These unresolved issues prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
